chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm has narrated from his father, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Bazzāz, from Ḥarīz, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “May I be made your ransom, how short is your remaining, O Ahl al-Bayt, and how near your terms are to one another, despite the people’s need for you.”

He said, “Indeed, for each one of us there is a scroll in which is what he needs to act upon during his appointed term. When what is in it from that which he was commanded has been completed, he knows that his appointed time has arrived. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) comes to him, announcing his death to him, and informs him of what awaits him with Allah.”

And al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) read his scroll that had been given to him, and what was to come of the announcement of his death was explained to him. Yet there remained in it matters not yet completed, so he went out for fighting. Among those matters that remained was that the angels had asked Allah concerning supporting him, and He gave them permission. They remained preparing themselves for fighting and making ready for that until he was killed. Then they descended, but his term had ended and he had been killed (عليه السلام).

So the angels said, ‘Our Lord, You gave us permission to descend and You gave us permission to support him, and we descended, but You had already taken him.’ Then Allah revealed to them, ‘Remain by his grave until you see him when he has come out; then support him. And weep for him and for what you missed of supporting him. Indeed, you have been singled out for supporting him and for weeping over him.’ So the angels wept in consolation and grief over what they had missed of supporting him. Then, when he comes out, they will be his supporters.”

key_terms.أَجَلَهُ: his appointed term or time of death
key_terms.صَحِيفَةً: a divinely given scroll containing the assigned duties of the Imam
key_terms.يَنْعَى: announces or conveys the news of death

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the short lifespans of the Ahl al-Bayt and the angels’ relation to Imam al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that each Imam has a divinely assigned scroll containing what he must carry out within his appointed term, and when that duty is completed, he knows his death has arrived. It also describes that Imam al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) proceeded according to this divine command, and that the angels were instructed to remain connected to his cause, mourning him and awaiting his return to support him.
